record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: For the same quadratic polynomial P_α(z) = exp(2πiα)z + z² with α a Bruno irrational and S_α its maximal Siegel singular disk, does there exist such an α for which the boundary ∂S_α is not a Jordan curve?

evidence.quote: Does there exist α2 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα2 (the boundary of Sα2) is not a Jordan curve ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each irrational number $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, consider the quadratic polynomial
$$P_\alpha(z)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}z+z^2,\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}.$$
The origin is a fixed point of $P_\alpha$ with multiplier $e^{2\pi i\alpha}$. Recall that $\alpha$ is a Bruno (Brjuno) number if, writing $p_n/q_n$ for the convergents of the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$, one has
$$\sum_{n\ge 0}\frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}<\infty.$$
By a theorem of Bruno (with sharpness due to Yoccoz in the quadratic case), whenever $\alpha$ is Bruno the map $P_\alpha$ is linearizable at $0$; the maximal Siegel disk $S_\alpha$ is the maximal open neighborhood of $0$ on which $P_\alpha$ is conformally conjugate to the rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$.

Question: Does there exist a Bruno irrational $\alpha$ such that the topological boundary $\partial S_\alpha$ of the maximal Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$ is not a Jordan curve?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question for all Bruno numbers appears to remain open. Significant partial progress exists: Yang (arXiv:1608.04106) proved that for irrationals of sufficiently high type satisfying the Bruno condition, the boundary of the quadratic Siegel disk is a Jordan curve. Buff–Chéritat constructed Bruno α for which ∂S_α is a smooth Jordan curve. No known result produces a Bruno α with non-Jordan Siegel-disk boundary, and the full classification is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: The high type quadratic Siegel disks are Jordan domains
status_evidence.snippet: For irrationals of sufficiently high type satisfying the Bruno condition, the boundary of the Siegel disk Δα of P_α(z)=e^{2πiα}z+z² is a Jordan curve.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: high-type Bruno numbers yield Jordan-curve boundaries.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Siegel disks with smooth boundaries (Buff–Chéritat)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of Bruno α for which the boundary of the Siegel disk of P_α is a C^∞ Jordan curve.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of Bruno α with smooth Jordan-curve Siegel boundary, but the full topological question for all Bruno α is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Is the boundary of a Siegel disk a Jordan curve?
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/article discussing the long-standing question of whether Siegel-disk boundaries are Jordan curves.
status_evidence.claim: The Jordan-curve question for Siegel-disk boundaries is recognized as a long-standing open problem.
